ch57.anchor: called Kyorōsan, which Toshizō had left with him
ch57.note: The Hijikata family, makers of the patent bruise-and-fracture medicine Ishida Powder met early in the book, also sold this Kyorōsan as a cure for consumption. It was worthless against tuberculosis; Toshizō’s flat “It works” is the gift of a friend, not a physician’s prescription, and Okita takes it as such.

ch57.anchor: the Kiku-ichimonji blade Sōji had carried in Kyoto
ch57.note: The Kiku-ichimonji (“chrysanthemum and single line”) was a famous line of swords of the Ichimonji school of Bizen, whose smiths were granted the chrysanthemum crest. That Okita carried so fine a blade is a cherished tradition rather than a documented fact; Shiba keeps it, and lets the dying man clasp it at the last.

ch57.anchor: on Keiō 4, the thirtieth day of the fifth month, in that shed
ch57.note: Okita Sōji died at the Sendagaya nursery on Keiō 4/5/30 (19 July 1868), of the tuberculosis that had wasted him since the Kyoto years; his exact age is uncertain, his birth year being given variously as 1842 or 1844. That he died without ever learning of Kondō’s execution, as the following lines have it, is a much-repeated tradition rather than an established fact, but it fits the circumstances: he lay bedridden and hidden through the very weeks in which Kondō was taken and beheaded.

ch57.anchor: The original is in classical Chinese
ch57.note: The short memorial just quoted was composed in kanbun, formal literary Chinese, long the language of record and epitaph in Japan much as Latin was in Europe. The English here follows its measured, classical cadence.

ch57.anchor: The perpetual-memorial fee was five ryō
ch57.note: An eitai shidō-ryō was a lump sum paid to a temple to endow perpetual memorial services: prayers and offerings kept up on the death-anniversaries, in return for the gift, for as long as the temple stood. Five ryō was a modest endowment; the two hundred yen paid when the stone was rebuilt seventy years later was, as the text notes, a considerable sum for its day.
